# ⏰ ceichas [![Matrix](https://img.shields.io/badge/chat-%23pimalaya-blue?style=flat&logo=matrix&logoColor=white)](https://matrix.to/#/#pimalaya:matrix.org) [![Mastodon](https://img.shields.io/badge/news-%40pimalaya-blue?style=flat&logo=mastodon&logoColor=white)](https://fosstodon.org/@pimalaya)

Wait until a wall-clock time, counting suspended time and following clock changes

## Features

- **Wall-clock times**: waits until a date and time, not for a duration.
- **Suspend-aware**: a time passing while the machine sleeps is reached as soon as it resumes.
- **Clock changes followed**: a clock set past the time ends the wait, a clock set back keeps it going.
- **Wakeable**: another thread ends a wait at any moment, and a wake sent between two waits is never lost.
- **Native OS timers**: timerfd on Linux and Android, waitable timers on Windows, dispatch timers on macOS, and a one-second polling fallback everywhere else.
- **Never wakes a sleeping machine**: the timer waits for the machine, never rouses it.

## Usage

The whole API is documented on [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/ceichas/latest/ceichas), with a runnable snippet at the crate root.

The `cli` feature builds a `ceichas` binary, a `sleep` until a wall-clock time:

```sh
cargo install --git https://github.com/pimalaya/ceichas --features cli
ceichas 2026-11-06T08:45:00+01:00 && mpv alarm.ogg
ceichas --verbose +1h30m
```

It takes an RFC 3339 datetime, `+` and a duration in `s`, `m`, `h` and `d`, or a UNIX time, exits 0 once the time is reached and 1 on an error. The Binaries workflow builds it for Linux, macOS and Windows as workflow artifacts.

## Examples

[examples/at.rs](examples/at.rs) waits until a UNIX time, or a number of seconds from now, then prints how the wait ended and when. The NixOS VM test of [nix/vm-test.nix](nix/vm-test.nix) runs it around clock changes and suspends, and [tests/timer.rs](tests/timer.rs) runs the timer suite against every backend.
